Subject: NovusAI: p95/p99 latency probe scheduling + acceptance checklist

Hi Laura — great call earlier, thanks for the time. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before engineering starts the probe: 

Summary of ask
- NovusAI needs p95 <= 120ms and p99 <= 350ms for single-shot text generation (average prompt length ~120 tokens) across peak traffic patterns. Streaming endpoints should support chunked partial responses with no more than 80ms per chunk under expected concurrency.

Proposed probe scope
1) 72-hour continuous probe from a U.S. region (us-west) to capture diurnal variance.
2) Traffic envelope: baseline 150 rps steady-state, two 5-minute spikes to 450 rps to test autoscale and tail.
3) Input distribution: 70% single-turn generation (avg 120 tokens), 30% streaming chat (avg 220 tokens, streaming chunk size ~64 tokens).
4) Measurement points: end-to-end p95/p99 (client to client), per-segment breakdown (network, gateway, model inference, post-processing).

Engineering needs from NovusAI
- A stable endpoint (URL + auth) we can hit from our probe runners and your ops contact for quick troubleshooting.
- Any IP allowlist or token setup 24 hours before probe start.

Deliverables from Redwood
- Probe artifact: raw latency traces (per-request), aggregated p95/p99 tables, per-route histograms, and a short runbook of mitigations if we hit regressions.
- A recommended acceptance checklist with canary thresholds for go/no-go.

Timing
- Proposed start window: 2026-09-22 02:00 - 04:00 UTC (we'll coordinate exact start after allowlist/time confirmations).

Attachments
- novusai_slo_template.xlsx (SLO calc & traffic envelope)
- runbook_stub.md (probe runbook draft)

Open questions
- Do you have cross-region failover we should exercise, or should we keep probes to a single region first?
- For streaming: do you measure chunk latency at the gateway or at the client SDK?

Next steps
1) Laura / ops-eng: confirm endpoint + auth + IP allowlist by 2026-09-21 12:00 PDT.
2) Marissa: prep probe runners and share test harness by EOD 2026-09-21.
3) I'll book a 30m pre-probe call the morning of 2026-09-22 to ensure everyone is green.

Thanks — Rishi

Adding engineering details and a lightweight measurement plan — tagging here so Laura can see our approach: 

Probe runner topology
- Runners: 8 instances in us-west (mixed c6g and c7g), spread across two AZs to capture network variance.
- Collector: central aggregation in us-west-2 with per-request timing tags (client_send, gw_recv, gw_send, model_start, model_end, client_recv).

Traffic shaping and concurrency
- We'll replay the payload distribution you gave; the steady 150 rps will be achieved with 12 runner threads @ ~12.5 rps each.
- Spike windows: two 5-minute ramps to 450 rps with 30s linear ramp-up and ramp-down.

Streaming specifics
- For streaming chat: we'll instrument chunk arrival times and reassemble them to compute chunk-to-chunk latency and final response latency.
- If NovusAI can provide the SDK-instrumented client it will let us report true E2E; otherwise we'll rely on gateway timestamps and call that 'observed E2E' with a note.

Success / fail criteria (proposal)
- Pass: p95 <= 120ms AND p99 <= 350ms on single-shot during steady-state and no more than 1.5x p99 increase during spikes.
- Soft-fail (actionable): sustained p99 > 350ms for >20 minutes — triggers immediate mitigation playbook and model routing to smaller-quantized variant.

Logs / artifacts we will hand over
- csv of per-request events, aggregated histograms, Grafana snapshot links, and a short postmortem if we hit regressions.

I attached a stub runbook and a filled SLO template (lightly populated) — we'll iterate once ops-eng confirms the token/allowlist.

Marissa
